title: Graph-supported comparison for semilinear sum extension
statement:
Let $e:U\to T$ be a separated etale morphism of finite type of schemes, and choose a compactification $e=pj$ with $j:U\hookrightarrow\overline U$ quasi-compact open and $p:\overline U\to T$ proper. Let $R_1\leftarrow R_2\leftarrow\cdots$ be any inverse sequence of commutative rings. For each scheme use its small pro-etale site and constant ring sheaves $(R_n)$, and write $\mathscr S_Z$ for the category of strict semilinear module sections $M_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{n+1,n}M_n$ as in [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Let $e_{\Sigma!,\bullet}$ be levelwise sheafification of the direct-sum presheaf
$$V\longmapsto\bigoplus_{t:V\to U\,/T}M_n(V,t)$$
of [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf]. Its derived functor is the exact degreewise functor, denoted $De_{\Sigma!,\bullet}$.

The graph $\Gamma_t:V\to\overline U\times_TV$ of each lift $t$ is an open and closed immersion. The section equal to $m\in M_n(V,t)$ on this graph and zero on its complement is a section of $j_!M_n$ on $\overline U\times_TV$. The sum of these maps on the presheaf summands induces a module-sheaf map $e_{\Sigma!,\bullet}M\to p_{*,\bullet}j_{!,\bullet}M$, natural in $M$ and compatible with all pro-etale restrictions and semilinear transitions. Using the simultaneous derived operations and their comparison maps of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], the degreewise graph map followed by the derived direct-image comparison gives a natural transformation
$$\theta:De_{\Sigma!,\bullet}\longrightarrow Rp_{*,\bullet}j_{!,\bullet}$$
in the ordinary derived categories of sections. Its evaluation at $n$ is the analogous graph natural transformation of functors from $D(U_{\mathrm{proet}},R_n)$ to $D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},R_n)$. If $T,U,\overline U$ are separated of finite type over a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, $R_n$ is a finite ring killed by a power of a prime $\ell\ne p$, and the input is the etale pullback $\nu_U^*L$ of a bounded constructible finite-Tor complex, then $\theta_n$ equals the inverse of the finite etale sum-extension normalization of [lem-pur-etale-support-map-compatibility] transported via the specified compact-support comparison of [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility]. Here the sum-extension site comparison $\nu_T^*e_{\Sigma!}^{\mathrm{et}}\simeq e_{\Sigma!}^{\mathrm{proet}}\nu_U^*$ is the adjunction-preserving one obtained from the localized-site direct-image identification [lem-weil-pbc-localize-ringed-site-morphism]. This assertion specifies the graph map and its finite evaluation, without asserting it is an isomorphism on arbitrary inputs.

proof.text: The implemented infrastructure is proved directly. Vertical-slice sheaf gluing and continuity of composition on pro-etale sites prove sumSite_continuous and levelSite_continuous. Naturality of the sheafification adjunction in the coefficient ring gives coefficientMap_naturality, after uncurry of the inverse-sequence natural transformation. The universe-independent module pullback existence theorem supplies sumRestriction_isRightAdjoint. The graph factors as the section into V times_T U followed by the open base change of c.i; the section is open because the projection is etale. The graph is closed because its composite with the separated projection from V times_T c.Z is the identity. Finally, full faithfulness of precomposition with the homotopy-to-derived localization gives theta_existsUnique and levelTheta_existsUnique from their displayed natural representative words. proof.text:
For the finite clause put $A=R_n$. The adjunction-preserving isomorphism $\sigma$ of [lem-sp-et-proet-graph-sheaf-square] is the one specified in the item: its common right adjoint uses exactly the localized ringed-site identity and it preserves each lift summand. Its sheaf square and [lem-sp-graph-derived-mate-factorization] give, for a bounded representative $K$ of $L$ and $P=j_!K$,
$$\theta_n(\nu_U^*L)\sigma_L=Rp_*^{\mathrm{proet}}(o_L)b_{p,QP}\nu_T^*(\gamma_P^{\mathrm{et}}Q(G_K^{\mathrm{et}})).$$
Here $p$ is qcqs because it is proper; $P$ is bounded since open extension is exact. The chosen representative is bounded since $L$ is bounded.

proof.text:
The field $k$ is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0,k$), so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes all three schemes Noetherian. The finite ring hypothesis allows [lem-pur-etale-support-map-compatibility]: its inverse normalization is $\gamma_P^{\mathrm{et}}Q(G_K^{\mathrm{et}})=(c_e^{c,\mathrm{et}}(L))^{-1}$. By [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility], $Rp_*^{\mathrm{proet}}(o_L)b_{p,QP}=c_{e,A}^c(L)$ on the stated bounded constructible finite-Tor input; its field-characteristic and coefficient hypotheses are exactly those here. Substitution gives
$$\theta_n(\nu_U^*L)\sigma_L=c_{e,A}^c(L)\nu_T^*((c_e^{c,\mathrm{et}}(L))^{-1}).$$
This is the required transported inverse. The factorization is an equality of derived natural transformations, so this substitution proves the natural normalization, including its specified site comparison.
